news.title: USA exit U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
news.lede: Brazil advance to quarter-finals in Poland. Americans have not won tournament since 2012. US youth teams have struggled in recent showings. The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time.

news.title: Tuchel: England was 'waiting for death' in World Cup semifinal defeat
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel said that England were "waiting for death" in their World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as the Three Lions boss mounted another defence of his controversial substitutions. Tuchel is preparing to name his squad for England's first matches since the painful end of their World Cup campaign. But, ahead of Nations League matches against Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic, he revealed that he is still haunted by the pain of their failed bid to reach a first World Cup final since 1966. England blew the lead given to them by Anthony Gordon as late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez sealed Argentina's 2-1 victory.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel can't watch Argentina collapse back - but now accepts blame for agonising exit
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel has revealed he has still not been able to watch back England’s World Cup semi final defeat as it was an “agony of epic proportions.” England boss Tuchel admitted he went defensive too early against Argentina because he felt his side were waiting for “death” with the game slipping away from them. Tuchel was talking on the FA’s Reflections show and said he could only bring himself to watch clips of the game with his other coaches at St George’s Park last week. But Tuchel admitted that he has not watched the game in its entirety and, while reviewing the Argentina heartbreak, repeated back some commentary which he says summed it up.

news.title: James Rodríguez puts an end to his time with the Colombia National Team: reactions from the football world
news.lede: James Rodríguez announced his retirement from the Colombia National Team this Tuesday, bringing an end to a 15-year international career. The 35-year-old midfielder shared his decision through a video posted on his social media. The forward closes his chapter representing his country with 131 matches played and 31 goals. He featured in three World Cups and had one of his most memorable performances in Brazil 2014, a tournament in which he finished as the top scorer with six goals.
